text:
Matty Beniers has goals in three straight games and seven on the season, and he's now running Seattle's top power play with Jared McCann out until January. Alison Lukan, covering the Kraken, keeps noting his chemistry with Mackie Samoskevich. For a former Calder Trophy winner who has spent three years being measured against his rookie season, this is the version Seattle hoped for.

Some of it is real. He has 13 points in 21 games at nearly 18 minutes a night, and the Kraken's share of expected goals is 6.3 points better with him on the ice than off. Some of it is finishing: seven goals on 5.3 expected. He has only 31 shots, so the goal pace leans on good shooting. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) finds nothing far from a typical forward in his tracked games. Evolving-Hockey had him 58th among forwards in wins above replacement last season. Our range projects 41 to 61 points. The power-play role is his chance to push the top end.
